probe.name: wrong-grid-weights
probe.rationale: Inflates the normalized posterior mass of all 100 cells in the z=2.50 column by a uniform 0.2% and renormalizes. The 40,000 weights still sum to exactly 1, are finite and positive and every structural/coverage property holds, so the file parses and passes structure checks. But each z=2.5 cell's normed_exp_trans now deviates by ~2e-3 relative from the recomputed Part-1 cell mass, ~6 orders of magnitude beyond the declared 1e-8 relative tolerance, and the analytic_grid summary means (which I update in lockstep to keep summary_estimates_consistency passing against the submitter's own files) drift by ~5e-6/5.1e-6 relative from the true posterior means. This isolates the per-cell posterior-mass scientific rule: the cell identities, alpha/beta columns and row multiplicity are all preserved, so only analytic_grid_values must fail. Grid weights at z=2.5 carry substantial mass, so the shift is a real scientific change of the estimated marginal posterior in z.
probe.script:
import os
for f in ('analytic_posterior_grid.csv','pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv','posterior_mean_estimates.csv'):
    if os.path.exists(f):
        os.chmod(f, 0o644)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
g = pd.read_csv('analytic_posterior_grid.csv')
assert list(g.columns) == ['X','Z','alpha','beta','normed_exp_trans']
assert len(g) == 40000
zr = np.round(g.Z*100)/100
sel = np.isclose(zr, 2.5)
assert sel.sum() == 100 and g.loc[sel,'X'].nunique() == 100
# Inflate the posterior mass of the z=2.5 cell column by 0.2% and renormalize:
# the weights still sum to 1, are positive and finite, but no longer match the
# Part-1 posterior mass per cell (relative deviation ~2e-3 >> 1e-8 tolerance),
# and the analytic summary means drift by ~2e-3 relative.
w = g.normed_exp_trans.to_numpy().copy()
w[sel] *= 1.002
w = w / w.sum()
assert np.isfinite(w).all() and (w > 0).all()
assert abs(w.sum() - 1.0) < 1e-12
g['normed_exp_trans'] = w
g.to_csv('analytic_posterior_grid.csv', index=False)
print('rows', len(g), 'sum_w', w.sum(), 'shifted cells', int(sel.sum()))

probe.name: wrong-moments-biased-mean
probe.rationale: Applies the documented wrong-prior signature: the addendum states that sampling under the Part-1 prior without the HalfNormal envelope shifts the mean of alpha by about +20%, versus the 2.5% relative acceptance limit on the plain mean. Every alpha draw is multiplied by 1.20, keeping all draws strictly positive, all 8,000 (alpha, beta) rows distinct (a global positive rescaling cannot create collisions), chain/draw labels intact and 2,000 rows per chain, so mcmc_draws_structure still passes. The alpha sd also inflates by ~20% (limit 20% relative, so it fails marginally too), while beta's mean/sd and the Pearson correlation are untouched and remain valid. I recompute the pymc_mcmc alpha summary mean so summary_estimates_consistency holds against the submitter's own draw column, isolating the statistical-distribution rule.

# plausible wrong-prior submission whose plain mean is far outside the 2.5%

assert d.duplicated(subset=['alpha','beta']).sum() == 0

probe.name: wrong-prior-corr-collapse
probe.rationale: Destroys the sample's correlation structure while keeping its means and sds intact: each alpha draw is moved toward the rigid relation alpha = 5*beta, driving the sample Pearson correlation from ~0.92 to ~0.998 and pulling the pooled alpha mean from ~1.99 to ~11.4, while every draw stays strictly positive, all 8,000 rows stay distinct (a bijective continuous shift of distinct points), and labels and per-chain row counts are untouched. This isolates the declared |corr - exact corr| <= 0.15 acceptance limit (deviation ~0.08 exceeds it given the reference correlation of ~0.9228) while also failing the 2.5% mean limit, exercising the joint-moment validation of the Part-2 model rather than a parse or structure failure. The pymc_mcmc summary rows are recomputed from the mutated draws so cross-file consistency holds.

old.to_csv('posterior_mean_estimates.csv', index=False)

probe.name: rep-grid-x-artifact-string
probe.rationale: Replaces one actual stepwise-grid floating-point artifact (verified in the reference: X = -2.2800000000000002 at grid cell x=-2.28, z=1.00) with the exact hundredth string '-2.28'. The decoded coordinate differs from the original value by less than 1e-15, far inside the 1e-6 lattice-alignment bound, and the public text explicitly accepts both the artifact and fewer-digit prints of the same cell. The row is rewritten as the single quoted cell within an otherwise untouched file, so weights, values, coverage and summary means are unchanged and all checks must still pass.
probe.script:
import os
for f in ('analytic_posterior_grid.csv','pymc_ab_posterior_draws.csv','posterior_mean_estimates.csv'):
    if os.path.exists(f):
        os.chmod(f, 0o644)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
g = pd.read_csv('analytic_posterior_grid.csv')
assert len(g) == 40000 and g.X.notna().all() and g.Z.notna().all()
# Verify an actual stepwise-grid artifact value, then replace it with the exact
# hundredth string: the decoded coordinate is within 1e-15 of the same original
# full-precision value, matching the same cell far inside the 1e-6 bound.
xr = np.round(g.X*100)/100
rows = g.index[(np.abs(g.X - xr) > 0) & (np.abs(g.X - xr) < 1e-9)]
assert len(rows) > 0
j = int(rows[0])
raw = float(g.loc[j,'X']); xj = float(xr[j])
assert abs(raw - xj) < 1e-9
fmt = '%.2f' % xj
assert abs(float(fmt) - raw) < 1e-9
X = g.X.astype(object)
X[j] = fmt
out = g.copy()
out['X'] = X
out.to_csv('analytic_posterior_grid.csv', index=False)
print('cell', j, 'raw', repr(raw), '->', fmt)
